_comment: Copy rulings that authorize a customer-facing GDPR letter, one record per ruling. This file is the ONLY source the
send gate trusts for a ruling id: adding one is a reviewed commit, never an edit on a host. `kind` must match the
letter being sent (ask|confirm), `expires` bounds it, and `source` says where the ruling was issued so a reader can
check the words rather than our summary of them.

rulings.source: firstmate inbox 027 (Fable driver, single sender seat), ruling against gdpr-ruling-for-jan s1-2 + gdpr-ack-v2 s2 step 1
firstmate inbox 027: 'APPROVED AS WRITTEN, approval id fable-ruling-1103-d2/gdpr-progress-line'

Fable ruling B3 (data/verify-sla-driver-fable-d2/rulings-blockers-1103-20Z.md): wire confirm/ask through the approved sender adapter; copy = the already-approved erasure-confirmation template (firstmate 943) + gdpr-ack-v2 s2, verbatim

firstmate inbox 099/102, Fable close-out ruling [key=gdpr-support-from-1104]: notices@/legal@ requests are answered from support@ as a NEW thread (conditions 1-6), implemented in hydra #1749. SCOPE IS THE MAILBOX ROUTE, NOT THE INTERCOM ONE, and the subject is CLASS-SCOPED: copy.NEW_THREAD_SUBJECT_APPROVED_CLASSES is ('privacy_erasure',), so naming this ruling for an access/correction/objection row does NOT authorize its subject. The one-line lead is its own GO (legal-finalize-fable-k1, 2026-11-04) and its own constant, copy.NEW_THREAD_LEAD_APPROVED.

Fable decisions board 11-04 (Aaron 2026-11-04 ~21:1xZ delegation: 'use fable to make the decisions waiting on me ... stop waiting on me'; data/captain-decisions-fable-d6/decisions-2026-11-04.md) row B26 Q1: 'unlock both lines; the register sends on its due dates (copy already approved in gdpr-ack-v2-and-arpad-1101.md)' and row B27 THREE: 'merge the hide batch and schedule the tick (unlock)'. Marked IRREVERSIBLE (customer-facing legal sends): executes 24h after the board (not_before 2026-11-05T21:30Z) unless Aaron vetoes. STANDING = the scheduled path (gdpr_pipeline.approval.verify_standing) because an hourly tick cannot post a 2h Slack approval per batch; the interactive grammar path is unchanged and this record cannot loosen it.
rulings.copy_sha_note: copy.fingerprint() over every customer-facing constant + the copy gates. A standing grant runs unattended for a month, so it names the words it was cut for: editing any approved sentence or flipping a gate changes this value and the tick REFUSES until a PR re-cuts it. Re-cut with `gdpr-pipeline.py copy-sha`. RE-CUT 2026-11-06 (hydra #1779): the identity now also covers the `ASK` mapping the sender actually reads, the renderers' behaviour and the helpers they reach, and the new-thread assembler itself (which moved out of send.py so this identity can cover it), so the value moved while no approved sentence changed - the words are identical, the grant just names them more precisely.
rulings.classes_note: The request CLASSES this grant authorises, checked by verify_standing against every item in the batch. A kind-only grant was not enough (QA finding on #1779): `copy.ASK` is ERASURE copy, and a dmca_takedown or legal_threat row reaches the same ASK_LINK verdict, so the first unattended tick would have told a rights-holder that 'the deletion request you made' is in progress. Measured on the live register 2026-11-06: 5 dmca_takedown and 30 legal_threat rows carry ASK_LINK, 15 of them already past due. Widening this list releases customer-facing copy, so it is widened in the PR that carries that class's ruling.
